name: Rooted Failure Transfers to an Exact Edge Profile
statement: Let $0\in C\subseteq A,B$ be ample, with $A\cap B=C$, ample union, and $\operatorname{Sh}(A)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(B)=\operatorname{Sh}(C)$. Suppose $C$ is dismantlable ample, both wings peel to $C$, and both admit acyclic USOs with sink $0$. For a fresh coordinate, form the two-layer family $L=(A\times\{0\})\cup(B\times\{1\})$ and mark the vertical edge $D$ over $0$. Then $L$ is ample and its edge profile is $(p,1,1,p,p)$, where $p=1$ exactly when $C$ peels to $0$. Thus when rooted peeling of $C$ fails, either endpoint of $D$ is an attainable sink, but the edge cannot be retained and neither endpoint can be deleted first as a leaf.
proof: Supports avoiding the new coordinate are counted by the ample union, while supports containing it correspond exactly to the common shadow of $A$ and $B$, proving ampleness. Clearing one wing relative to $C$, then its copy of $C$, and finishing in the other wing gives either endpoint as a sink. If $C$ peels to $0$, clear both wings and lift that rooted order to retain $D$ or exit through either leaf. Conversely, in any retention or leaf-exit peeling, record the moment when each full vertical fiber first breaks. The projected corner cubes give a corner reduction of $C$ to $0$; connectivity handles the leaf-exit terminal state. Hence each of the other three profile entries equals the rooted-peeling bit $p$.
